prerequisites: Knowledge of contents typical of Mathematics I and II of high school, including elementary algebra, trigonometry, and basic calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for solving mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra.
Utilize the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces, and linear applications, and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces through scalar product, norm, or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and space.
Identify the basic elements of differential equations and systems of differential equations and use algebraic tools to solve elementary cases.

syllabus_topics: Basic properties and fundamental operations of real and complex numbers.
Resolution of systems using Gauss Elimination Method. Application to inverse matrix calculation.
Linear combinations and linear independence. Bases and dimension. Coordinates.
Definition and properties of linear applications.
Kernel and image of an application. Classification of linear applications.
Applications to solving systems of linear differential equations.
Euclidean vector space. Scalar product and metric properties.
Matrix calculation and systems of equations
Vector spaces and change of basis
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.15*NL + maximum (0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC), where NL is the laboratory practice grade, NA the classroom practice grade, and NC the average of two written partial controls. To pass, a minimum of 2.5 out of 10 points is required in each partial control; otherwise, the final numerical grade will be the minimum of NF and 4.5. Extraordinary calls include a two-part written exam and a laboratory practice test, using the same grading formula. Grades for classroom practices are valid for the entire academic year, while laboratory practice grades can be conserved or replaced by a new specific exam.
